fields.statement: QA built ./cmd/rhiza to a scratch path and, in a scratch root, ran rhiza request 'first idea' --note (CRLF, multi-line Markdown with outer blank lines) --note second --json: both notes stored oldest first in requests.json and request ls --json, lines kept, CRLF to LF, outer blank trimmed; request ls text shows [2 notes]/[1 note]; a request with no notes writes no notes key. Blank and empty --note (exit 2 'is empty'), 8001 bytes (exit 2 'is 8001 bytes, at most 8000') queue nothing; 8000 bytes accepted.

QA with a scratch build: rhiza request note <8-char prefix> 'third\r\nline two' appended a third note (printed with all notes, CRLF to LF); --dry-run --json showed the would-be note and requests.json stayed unchanged; unknown ID, 3-char prefix, ambiguous prefix, blank and 9000-byte notes, missing args and a drawn request (Run set, human and --json) were each usage errors (exit 2) with requests.json byte-identical; after a real daemon --once drew the run, note was refused as no longer queued.

QA with a scratch build and fake rex/claude: queued a request with two --note values (one multi-line Markdown) plus a third via request note, rhiza daemon --once drew its run, run start --foreground --request ran the plan workflow; the planner's brief.md had ## Request notes right after ## Change set, the lead sentence and Note 1..3 verbatim in order, then ## Leaves. A plan run with no request had no Request notes section. go test ./internal/run ./internal/daemon -run Brief|Request, ./internal/api -run Request and the request-notes-brief, describe-golden, plan-requests, brief-files scripts pass.
